Let \(v=\binom n3\). The Smith normal form of \(L_n\) is

\[
\operatorname{diag}\Big(
\underbrace{1,\ldots,1}_{q+1},
\underbrace{2,\ldots,2}_{2n-4},
6,6,
\underbrace{c,\ldots,c}_{r},
\underbrace{b,\ldots,b}_{q},
\underbrace{a,\ldots,a}_{n-2},
0
\Big),
\]

where

\[
m=\binom n2,\qquad q=m-2n+1,\qquad r=\binom n3-2m+n,
\]
and
\[
c=3(n-2),\qquad b=2(n-1)c,\qquad a=\frac n4\,b.
\]

These are in divisibility order because \(n\equiv0\pmod {12}\), so \(6\mid c\), \(c\mid b\), and \(b\mid a\).

Thus explicitly the invariant factors are

\[
\boxed{
1^{\,q+1},\;
2^{\,2n-4},\;
6^{\,2},\;
c^{\,r},\;
b^{\,q},\;
a^{\,n-2},\;
0
}.
\]
